messages.content:
The pump is running but I notice flow is dropping. Looking at the discharge pressure and checking the suction line.
Evidence (readings): discharge pressure normal; suction strainer delta three times clean value

Per the provided readings: discharge pressure normal and suction strainer delta is three times clean — mechanical restriction on suction side explains the low flow. Safety floor: isolate and follow LOTO before opening; no energized work. Next step: clean or swap the strainer, then re-take readings to confirm they return to baseline before closing.

I hear a rattle from the bearing side when the fan spins. Took a reading and the vibration signature is elevated. Air pressure downstream looks normal.
Evidence (readings): bearing acceleration two point five times baseline; discharge air pressure unchanged

Per the provided readings: bearing vibration is two point five times baseline while air pressure remains unchanged — bearing drag explains the mechanical noise and thermal rise. Safety floor: LOTO the motor and allow it to cool; no energized work. Next step: check coupling alignment and bearing play, then re-measure vibration to confirm baseline.

Pump discharge is climbing. Flow is down slightly. Current draw went up.
Evidence (readings): pump discharge pressure twenty-eight psi above normal; pump motor current eighteen percent high; water flow two percent low

Per the provided readings: pump discharge pressure is twenty-eight psi over normal and flow is two percent low — outlet blockage explains the pressure rise and flow loss. Safety floor: de-energize the pump and relieve system pressure; lockout the starter. Next step: check outlet isolation valve and strainers, then re-take readings to confirm baseline.

The cylinder is moving slowly and there's oil around the rod. System pressure is lower than expected.
Evidence (readings): system pressure five psi lower than spec; cylinder rod area has visible oil seep; advance speed twenty percent slower

Per the provided readings: system pressure is five psi below specification and advance speed is twenty percent slow while rod area shows oil seepage — rod seal leakage explains both symptoms. Safety floor: relieve hydraulic pressure using manual vent; lockout the pump. Next step: replace the rod seal, replenish oil, then re-measure to confirm baseline.

asset: the air-cooled condenser on the refrigerant loop

messages.content:
The fins look dusty and condensing is not working right. Outlet temperature is high. Fan motor is running normal current.
Evidence (readings): condenser outlet pressure eight psi above design; fan motor current unchanged; condenser surface temp twenty-four degrees above ambient

Per the provided readings: condenser discharge pressure is eight psi over design and surface temperature is twenty-four degrees above ambient — fouled fins explain both the pressure and temperature rise. Safety floor: de-energize the fan motor before cleaning; isolate the refrigerant loop. Next step: clean condenser fins, then re-measure pressure and temperature to confirm baseline.

The valve is sluggish. Air is escaping from the vent port. Pilot pressure is low when I measured it.
Evidence (readings): pilot pressure twelve psi below normal; shift time forty percent slower; air escaping audibly from vent port

Per the provided readings: pilot pressure is twelve psi below normal and mechanical shift time is forty percent slow — pilot seal leak reduces the pressure differential needed. Safety floor: lockout the air supply at solenoid; release all stored pressure. Next step: inspect pilot seals and passages, replace seals if worn, then re-measure to confirm baseline.

The primary side is getting hot. The secondary is not performing right. Current is unbalanced between phases.
Evidence (readings): primary coil surface temp thirty-two degrees over normal; secondary winding resistance fifteen percent high; current imbalance eleven percent

Per the provided readings: primary coil temperature is thirty-two degrees above normal and secondary winding resistance is fifteen percent high — incipient short in secondary winding explains the heat rise and resistance change. Safety floor: de-energize the welder and allow cooling; lockout the starter. Next step: perform insulation resistance test, then verify baseline before resuming welding.

The compressor is not pulling a proper vacuum and the discharge line temperature is cool. Pressure is off.
Evidence (readings): discharge line temperature eighteen degrees below baseline; discharge pressure five psi lower than design; motor current four percent below baseline

Per the provided readings: discharge temperature is eighteen degrees below baseline and discharge pressure is five psi low — leaky discharge valve explains the pressure loss and cooler discharge. Safety floor: de-energize the compressor and isolate; lockout the motor. Next step: replace discharge valve cartridge, then re-measure to confirm baseline.

The compressor is outputting less air than it should. The discharge air is hotter than normal. Motor current is normal.
Evidence (readings): discharge air flow six percent below normal; discharge air temperature twenty-eight degrees above standard; motor current remains nominal

Per the provided readings: discharge flow is six percent low and outlet temperature is twenty-eight degrees above standard — internal leakage explains flow loss and heat rise. Safety floor: lockout the compressor before opening; no energized work. Next step: inspect rotor and stator surfaces for wear, replace worn seals, then re-measure to confirm baseline.

The chain is hanging loose. Motor is pulling more current. Conveyor is running slow.
Evidence (readings): chain deflection five inches at midspan (should be one inch); motor current twenty-two percent above baseline; conveyor speed nine percent slow

Per the provided readings: motor current is twenty-two percent above baseline and chain deflection is five inches at midspan — chain stretch and misalignment explain the load rise and speed reduction. Safety floor: LOTO the drive motor and support the load; no energized work. Next step: adjust chain tension, re-align sprockets, then verify motor current and deflection return to baseline.

Pump is making noise and vibrating. Water flow is low. Suction side pressure is too low.
Evidence (readings): inlet pressure four psi below atmospheric; outlet pressure eight psi below normal; discharge flow fourteen percent low; audible rattling

Per the provided readings: inlet pressure is four psi below atmospheric while discharge flow is fourteen percent below normal — cavitation explains both pressure loss and flow reduction. Safety floor: isolate the pump from supply lines; no energized work near inlet. Next step: check suction strainer for blockage, clean or replace, then re-measure to confirm baseline.

The servo loop is oscillating. Position is off. Current spikes are happening when it should be smooth.
Evidence (readings): servo loop current spikes to eighteen amps (baseline fourteen); position lag zero point two-five inch; encoder resolution errors on feedback

Per the provided readings: servo motor current spikes reach eighteen amps while position lag is confirmed at zero point two-five inches — encoder signal corruption explains both symptoms. Safety floor: de-energize servo drive before accessing encoder; lockout main disconnect. Next step: inspect and reseat encoder signal connectors, test encoder output, then verify baseline.

The pump sounds wrong. Flow is down. Discharge pressure is low. There's a grinding noise from the pump inlet.
Evidence (readings): discharge pressure sixteen psi below design; discharge flow eight percent low; audible grinding from pump inlet

Per the provided readings: discharge pressure is sixteen psi below design and flow is eight percent low while grinding noise emanates from inlet — impeller blade damage explains all symptoms. Safety floor: de-energize and isolate pump; lockout motor. Next step: remove pump cover and impeller, inspect blade edges for pitting, replace if damaged, then re-measure to confirm baseline.

One bearing is running hotter than the other side. Vibration is present at bearing frequencies. Motor current is up.
Evidence (readings): bearing temperature forty-four degrees above the non-drive bearing; vibration at bearing frequencies three point two times baseline; motor current thirteen percent above normal

Per the provided readings: bearing temperature is forty-four degrees above the opposite end and vibration at bearing frequencies is three point two times baseline — bearing misalignment explains both thermal and mechanical symptoms. Safety floor: de-energize kiln drive motor; lockout the starter. Next step: measure coupling runout with dial indicator, realign motor or gearbox, then verify baseline.

The RO module needs more pressure than before. Flow output is down. Concentrate line pressure is high.
Evidence (readings): feed pressure thirty-two psi above previous baseline; membrane outlet flux twelve percent below design; concentrate line pressure eighteen psi above normal

Per the provided readings: feed pressure is thirty-two psi above baseline and concentrate pressure is eighteen psi high while membrane flux is twelve percent below design — membrane fouling explains both pressure rise and flux loss. Safety floor: de-energize feed pump and close isolation valves; no high-pressure work. Next step: perform chemical cleaning cycle using scale dissolver, then re-measure to confirm baseline.

The outlet air is humid. Pressure drop is higher than normal. The cartridge feels room temperature.
Evidence (readings): outlet air humidity sixty-eight percent (should be below five); outlet pressure eighty-seven psi vs inlet ninety-two psi (normal drop two); cartridge temperature room temp

Per the provided readings: outlet humidity is sixty-eight percent versus design spec below five percent and pressure drop is five psi instead of normal two psi — saturated adsorbent cartridge explains both symptoms. Safety floor: de-energize heater cartridge and isolate dryer; no energized work. Next step: perform regeneration cycle or replace cartridge if end-of-life, then re-measure to confirm baseline.

The spool is stuck. Pilot pressure is down. Tank return line has back-pressure.
Evidence (readings): pilot pressure eleven psi below spec; tank return line pressure eight psi above baseline; spool detent positions stuck

Per the provided readings: pilot pressure is eleven psi below specification and tank pressure is eight psi above baseline — blockage in spool center explains both pilot loss and tank back-pressure. Safety floor: relieve hydraulic pressure using manual vent; lockout pump. Next step: remove spool cartridge and clean all passages, backflush tank return line, then verify baseline.

asset: the electric motor in the water treatment aeration system

messages.content:
The motor case has condensation. Insulation resistance is very low. The motor is not running right.
Evidence (readings): phase-to-ground insulation resistance zero point eight megohm (should be above ten); motor case has condensation on windings visible

Per the provided readings: phase-to-ground insulation resistance is zero point eight megohm versus minimum ten megohm specification and condensation is visible on windings — moisture degraded insulation and created partial-phase leakage. Safety floor: de-energize motor immediately; lockout motor starter. Next step: allow motor to dry in warm low-humidity environment for twenty-four hours, then re-test insulation to confirm above ten megohm.

The oil looks darker and thinner compared to the maintenance log photo. Gearbox case is hot. Pump discharge pressure is down.
Evidence (readings): oil color darker and thinner than monthly record photo; gearbox case temperature thirty-two degrees above baseline; pump discharge pressure seven psi lower than normal

Per the provided readings: gearbox case temperature is thirty-two degrees above baseline and pump discharge pressure is seven psi low — oil degradation reduced viscosity. Safety floor: stop blender immediately and de-energize; lockout motor before draining oil. Next step: drain gearbox, flush system with correct new fluid grade, then measure case temperature to confirm baseline.

The cold side is not getting cold. Shell-side pressure drop is higher than when I checked it last month.
Evidence (readings): cold-side outlet temperature eleven degrees below previous baseline for same inlet; shell-side pressure drop fifteen psi above baseline

Per the provided readings: cold-side outlet temperature is eleven degrees below baseline and shell-side pressure drop is fifteen psi above normal — internal tube-side or shell-side fouling explains reduced heat transfer and pressure drop. Safety floor: de-energize heater circuit and isolate exchanger; close isolation valves. Next step: perform chemical cleaning cycle using approved scale dissolver, then re-measure to confirm baseline.

messages.content:
Bearing is warm.
Evidence (readings): bearing temperature elevated two degrees above normal; motor current baseline; discharge flow nominal.

Per the provided readings: bearing temperature is elevated while motor current and discharge flow remain baseline — mild thermal condition suggests early bearing wear or lubrication degradation. Safety floor: de-energize equipment and allow to cool; lockout drive motor. Next step: inspect bearing seals for contamination, verify lubrication level and condition, then monitor temperature and current to confirm they stabilize before resuming normal operation.
